title: Decent Grinder, Hard on the Hands
text:
Decent Grinder, Hard on the Hands. I like this grinder, it produces a perfect grind for my French press. However if you want a super fine grind for espresso you're not likely to get it. You change the grind by tightening the top knob that also holds the handle on. This means each time you refill the whole bean container you're going to have to guess how tight you had it beforehand. It's a little aggravating because there's no set grind levels. Your grind will be different every time.

I'm disabled and have some serious nerve damage in my hands as well as arthritis trouble just about everywhere. Today, the third time I used this grinder, I wanted to make two large mugs of coffee. I had to open and put whole beans in the grinder three times. Unscrew the small and somewhat hard to remove knob. Remove the cap and handle then fill the cylinder with beans then put it all back together to spend several minutes grinding away. After I was done with my third cycle I was pretty sore but I did get a couple great cups of coffee for my efforts.

In the end it works okay, again for a grind great for a French press, which I think is the best way to make coffee. It can give you the sense of accomplishment to hand grind your own beans and it is a bit more gentle on the beans. But it's a lot of effort in the morning. Me? I'll used up the bag of whole beans I bought to test this with and then I think I'm going back to buying fresh ground coffee.
I received this item in exchange for my review.
